value: ⚠️ EXACT COLUMNS ONLY: customers: [Id, FirstName, LastName], goods: [Id, Flavor, Food, Price], items: [Receipt, Ordinal, Item], receipts: [ReceiptNumber, Date, CustomerId]
Always use: customers c, receipts r, items i, goods g
⚠️ CRITICAL: When accessing columns from a CTE, YOU MUST use columns that were explicitly defined in the CTE's SELECT clause. Common error: Using g.Food when the CTE only selected Product
⚠️ CRITICAL: Reference CTE fields using CTE name (CustomerCTE.FirstName), NEVER using original table aliases (c.FirstName) in outer queries
⚠️ CRITICAL: In CTEs, explicitly SELECT every column you need in outer queries. If you need g.Food later, include it in the CTE's SELECT clause
When using AS to create aliases, reference the aliases exactly as defined. If you use 'AS FullName', reference it as 'FullName' not as 'Name'
When grouping by a complex expression with CASE, either repeat the EXACT expression or use a column alias
⚠️ CRITICAL: Use SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) for day extraction. NEVER use position 2
CASE CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday'... END
CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) % 7 IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END
CASE WHEN CAST(SUBSTR(r.Date, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) <= 10 THEN 'Early October'... END
⚠️ When using CASE in SELECT, you must repeat the EXACT SAME CASE expression in GROUP BY. Copy and paste the entire expression to ensure they match
If question asks for 'top X', INCLUDE 'LIMIT X' in your query
Always include primary keys when returning entities: c.Id for customers, g.Id for goods, r.ReceiptNumber for receipts
'Most popular' = COUNT(*), 'Most revenue' = SUM(g.Price)
AVG per transaction: WITH ReceiptTotals AS (SELECT i.Receipt, SUM(g.Price) AS Total FROM items i JOIN goods g ON i.Item = g.Id GROUP BY i.Receipt) SELECT AVG(rt.Total)...
When comparing groups (weekday vs weekend), use identical calculations for each group
JOIN items i1 JOIN items i2 ON i1.Receipt = i2.Receipt AND i1.Item < i2.Item
Customer product variety: Return COUNT(DISTINCT g.Id), COUNT(DISTINCT g.Food), AND COUNT(DISTINCT g.Flavor)
⚠️ Columns are only accessible in their scope. In nested queries, reference only columns from: 1) tables joined in that scope, or 2) columns explicitly selected in outer queries
Items sold by category: COUNT(*) grouped by g.Food
Revenue by category: SUM(g.Price) grouped by g.Food
Use simple aliases without spaces or special characters: 'AS PurchaseCount' not 'AS Purchase Count'
⚠️ CRITICAL: When copying data between queries, ensure the selected columns are identical. Don't reference a column unless it was explicitly selected
When using WITH clause, ensure all referenced CTEs are defined. Don't reference a CTE that isn't defined
⚠️ In JOIN conditions, only reference columns that exist in the tables being joined. Don't use CustomerCTE.Id in a JOIN if CustomerCTE doesn't have an Id field
